title: 例1：等距離点集合の上限を決める指数
section: 1. 研究数学の課題と実例
original:
For a real number \(p\in(1,\infty)\) and a positive integer \(n\), equip \(\mathbb R^n\) with the distance
\[
d_p(x,y)=\biggl(\sum_{j=1}^{n}|x_j-y_j|^p\biggr)^{1/p}.
\]
A finite subset \(S\subset\mathbb R^n\) is equilateral if there exists a real number \(r>0\) such that \(d_p(x,y)=r\) for every two distinct points \(x,y\in S\). Determine exactly the set of exponents \(p\in(1,\infty)\) for which, for every positive integer \(n\), every equilateral subset of \((\mathbb R^n,d_p)\) has at most \(n+1\) elements. Give the parameter set in interval notation.

A finite subset S⊂ℝ^n is equilateral if there exists a real number r>0 such that d_p(x,y)=r for every two distinct points x,y∈ S. title: 例4：再始動反復法の非収束
section: Appendix: 1. 研究分野の追加例
original:
For a positive integer \(s\), consider the following iteration in exact real arithmetic. Let \(n\ge1\), let \(A\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) satisfy \(A^\top=A\) and \(v^\top Av>0\) for every nonzero \(v\in\mathbb R^n\), and choose \(b,x_0\in\mathbb R^n\). Define
\[
x_*=A^{-1}b,\qquad r_k=b-Ax_k,\qquad \|v\|_A=(v^\top Av)^{1/2}.
\]
If \(r_k=0\), terminate. Otherwise, set
\[
\mathcal K_s(A,r_k)=\operatorname{span}\{r_k,Ar_k,\ldots,A^{s-1}r_k\}
\]
and let \(x_{k+1}\) be the unique minimizer of \(\|x_*-z\|_A\) over \(z\in x_k+\mathcal K_s(A,r_k)\). Each such minimization is one restart block, so \(k\) counts blocks. For a nonterminating orbit, define
\[
y_k=\frac{r_k}{\|r_k\|_2},\qquad \|v\|_2=(v^\top v)^{1/2}.
\]
Determine the smallest positive integer \(s\) for which there exist \(n,A,b,x_0\) as above such that \(r_k\ne0\) for every \(k\ge0\), but \((y_{2k})_{k\ge0}\) does not converge in Euclidean norm. Return \(+\infty\) if no such integer exists.

section: Appendix: 1. 研究分野の追加例
original:
Let \(I=\{4,6,8,\dots\}\cup\{\infty\}\). For each finite \(m\in I\), set
\[
R_m=\sqrt{\frac{2\pi}{m\sin(2\pi/m)}},
\]
and let \(P_m\subset\mathbb R^2\) be the interior of the convex hull of the points
\[
R_m\bigl(\cos((2k+1)\pi/m),\sin((2k+1)\pi/m)\bigr),\qquad k=0,\dots,m-1.
\]
Set \(P_\infty=\{x\in\mathbb R^2:\|x\|_2<1\}\). Thus every member of this family is a centrally symmetric convex domain of area \(\pi\).

For any domain \(\Omega\) in this family, define
\[
F_\Omega(\xi)=\int_\Omega e^{i\xi\cdot x}\,dx,\qquad
\kappa(\Omega)=\inf\{\|\xi\|_2:\xi\in\mathbb R^2,\ F_\Omega(\xi)=0\},
\]
where \(dx\) is planar Lebesgue measure, the inner product and norm are Euclidean, and \(\inf\varnothing=+\infty\).

Determine the unique maximizing index \(m_*\in I\) satisfying
\[
\kappa(P_{m_*})=\sup_{m\in I}\kappa(P_m).
\]

title: 例6：対称性を持たない最大円
section: Appendix: 1. 研究分野の追加例
original:
Work in the Euclidean plane with the lattice \(\mathbb Z^2\) of points having integer coordinates. All circles may have arbitrary real centers and positive radii. For a nonnegative integer \(n\), an \(n\)-circle is a circle whose open interior contains exactly \(n\) lattice points; lattice points on its circumference are not counted. An \(n\)-circle is called largest if its radius is at least the radius of every other \(n\)-circle. Call \(n\) strong if a largest \(n\)-circle exists but no largest \((n+1)\)-circle exists.

For a circle \(C\), let \(D(C)=C\cap\mathbb Z^2\) be its set of boundary lattice points. Say that \(D(C)\) has a mirror symmetry if reflection across some affine line in the plane maps \(D(C)\) onto itself.

Determine the smallest strong integer \(n\) for which there exists a largest \(n\)-circle \(C\) such that \(D(C)\) has no mirror symmetry.
